newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria's Black Widow sentenced to life in jail.
newsitem.headline: Austria's Black Widow sentenced to life in jail.

text.p: An Austrian court on Friday sentenced Elfriede Blauensteiner, dubbed the "Black Widow" by the media, to life imprisonment for poisoning an elderly male pensioner with fatal doses of medication.
The court in Krems, 50 km (30 miles) west of Vienna, found Blauensteiner, 66, guilty of the murder of 77-year-old Alois Pichler.
The jury reached its verdict at three a.m. (0200 GMT) after 12 hours of deliberation.
Although Blauensteiner was charged with only one murder, police are still investigating other deaths possibly linked to the bespectacled woman.

The case had all the elements of a Hollywood thriller. Blauensteiner was accused of placing advertisements in newspapers to meet rich, elderly men, allegedly poisoning her victims and then gambling away the money they left her in their wills.
Blauensteiner arrived last month for the start of the high-profile trial clutching a golden crucifix, claiming it was intended to protect her from vampires.
The matronly-looking woman said she enjoyed nursing pensioners through the autumn of their years and that it was a coincidence some of them subsequently died.

She was arrested in January last year, suspected of a murder spree spanning over a decade. Police have exhumed the corpses of three pensioners nursed by Blauensteiner, although one was too decomposed for forensic examination.
Police said she confessed to five murders, including that of her late husband Rudolf, during the initial investigation but later withdrew the confession.

She was charged with giving Pichler anti-depressants and diabetes medicine, leaving him in a room with the windows open all night and then putting him under a hot shower, which caused his fatal heart attack.

Doctors said a lethal dose of medicine was found in the body of Pichler, a widower and former postal worker from Lower Austria. He died in late 1995, just five weeks after he met Blauensteiner through a newspaper advertisement.
She admitted the wealth of prospective patients who replied to her advertisements was a definite factor in her choice. Pichler had a house with a garden and a healthy bank balance.
The judge sentenced Blauensteiner's former lawyer Harald Schmidt to seven years in jail for being an accomplice to grievous bodily harm and falsifying Pichler's will.
